chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ismāʿīl ibn Marrār, from Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام.
Concerning a mukātab who killed a man by mistake.

He said: “He is liable for the blood-money in proportion to the amount of him that has been freed, and his master is liable for what remains of the value of the slave. If the mukātab is unable, then he has no ʿāqilah; rather, that rests upon the Imam of the Muslims.”

key_terms.إِمَامِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Imam of the Muslims, the public authority responsible in this case
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: the slave property-status referred to in legal valuation
key_terms.دِيَتِهِ: the prescribed blood-money owed for the killing
key_terms.عَاقِلَةَ: the legally responsible agnatic support group that pays blood-money
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: a slave under a manumission contract

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the blood-money of a mukātab who kills someone by mistake?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a mukātab who commits accidental killing. Liability is divided according to the portion of freedom he has attained, with the remainder connected to his master, and if he cannot bear it, the responsibility goes to the Imam of the Muslims.
